name: Breedon Group plc
executive_summary: Breedon Group plc (BREE.L) screens as a strong buy on cheapness, dividend, GARP and risk metrics (9/22 models; composite 78%), anchored by P/B near 1.0, an ~8.7% FCF yield and a 4.3% dividend yield on a vertically integrated UK/Ireland/US construction materials platform with 1.7bn tonnes of mineral reserves. Filings show resilient cash generation—record post-Covid FCF of £133.2m in FY2025 and covenant leverage back to 1.8x—but earnings quality is cyclically diluted: like-for-like revenue fell 3% in 2025, GB volumes are in a fifth year of decline, and ROIC (7.8%) sits below management’s 10% medium-term target after Lionmark, Falling Springs and Booth. The valuation hook is a trough-cycle UK materials name trading near book with a progressive dividend and geographic diversification (Ireland and US offsetting GB weakness); the key debate is whether M&A-led growth and infrastructure/policy tailwinds (Irish NDP, US Midwest, UK CBAM advocacy) outweigh prolonged UK residential weakness and rising net debt (£690.5m at H1 2026; covenant leverage 2.1x).
investment_thesis:
The quantitative screen flags Breedon as a classic deep-value, income-plus-GARP candidate: it passes Deep Value, FCF Yield, Neff PEGY, High Dividend Yield, Dividend Growth, Dreman Contrarian, Composite Value, Earnings Quality and Financial Health, with full data quality (20/20 metrics). At P/E 14.5, P/B 1.0, EV/EBITDA 7.4 and FCF yield 8.7%, the market prices in cyclical stagnation rather than franchise durability.

Business quality supports the screen. Breedon is the largest British-based cement manufacturer, with quarry-to-customer vertical integration across GB, Ireland and the US, long-life reserves, and structurally higher margins in Ireland (~22% underlying EBITDA margin in FY2025 vs GB ~16.6%). Management has delivered self-help: over £20m of operational savings in 2025, FCF conversion at 48% (above the 45% target), and RCF extension to 2029/2030 plus low-coupon USPP funding. The progressive dividend (15.0p FY2025; interim raised 5% to 5.00p in H1 2026) is backed by cash, not optics.

For a value investor, the asymmetry is geographic optionality at a UK trough: Ireland revenue grew 12% in H1 2026; US like-for-like underlying EBITDA rose 14%, while GB remains flat to down. The screen’s risk-family pass is consistent with disclosed covenant headroom (leverage covenant 3.0x vs 2.1x at H1 2026), going-concern confirmation, and interest cover of 13.5x. Conviction on the screen is modest (38%) and timing neutral (RSI ~66), so the case is accumulate-on-weakness rather than chase momentum.
financial_review:
Primary source: UK RNS filing bodies (Final Results, 11 March 2026; Interim Results 2026, 29 July 2026; Trading Update, 20 November 2025). Yahoo (`financials_annual.json`) used only where noted for cross-check.

Annual results (year ended 31 December 2025 — Final Results RNS)

| Metric | FY2025 | FY2024 | Change |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Revenue | £1,713.8m | £1,576.3m | +9% |
| Like-for-like revenue | — | — | -3% |
| Underlying EBITDA | £278.8m | £269.9m | +3% |
| Underlying EBITDA margin | 16.3% | 17.1% | -80bps |
| Statutory PBT | £105.3m | £125.4m | -16% |
| Underlying PBT | £140.2m | £150.8m | -7% |
| Basic EPS | 24.2p | 28.1p | -14% |
| Underlying basic EPS | 31.8p | 34.4p | -8% |
| Dividend per share | 15.0p | 14.5p | +3% |
| Free Cash Flow (company definition) | £133.2m | £114.1m | +17% |
| FCF conversion | 48% | 42% | +6ppt |
| Net debt (incl. IFRS 16) | £527.3m | £405.3m | +30% |
| Covenant leverage | 1.8x | 1.4x | +0.4x |
| ROIC (post-tax) | 7.8% | 9.0% | -120bps |

Reported revenue growth was acquisition-led (Lionmark contributed £161.4m revenue and £21.1m underlying EBITDA in ten months). Organic GB volumes fell for a fourth consecutive year; ready-mixed concrete volumes were at their lowest since 1963. Underlying EBITDA still grew 3% on cost discipline and operational excellence. Statutory EPS fell on higher amortisation of acquired intangibles (£25.3m non-underlying) and increased finance costs (£29.7m vs £25.4m).

Cash performance was the standout: FCF of £133.2m was a record post-Covid, with leverage reduced 0.4x from the H1 2025 peak of 2.2x to 1.8x at year-end (target range 1.0–2.0x). Liquidity exceeded £245m (undrawn RCF >£130m plus cash >£115m). Impairment testing retained headroom in all three CGUs, with additional GB sensitivities.

Interim results (six months ended 30 June 2026 — Interim Results RNS)

| Metric | H1 2026 | H1 2025 | Change |
|--------|---------|---------|--------|
| Revenue | £857.9m | £815.9m | +5% |
| LFL revenue | — | — | +3% |
| Underlying EBITDA | £115.5m | £115.0m | Flat |
| LFL underlying EBITDA | — | — | +1% |
| Underlying EBITDA margin | 13.5% | 14.1% | -60bps |
| Statutory basic EPS | 7.4p | 8.0p | -16% |
| Underlying basic EPS | 9.4p | 11.2p | -16% |
| Interim dividend | 5.00p | 4.75p | +5% |
| Net debt | £690.5m | £648.1m | +7% |
| Covenant leverage | 2.1x | 2.2x | -0.1x |
| ROIC (LTM) | 7.0% | 7.8% | -80bps |

Geographic divergence intensified: GB revenue flat with underlying EBITDA -3%; Ireland revenue +12% (LFL +9%), underlying EBITDA +3%; US revenue +20% (LFL +13%), LFL underlying EBITDA +14%. H1 FCF was an outflow of £14.6m (seasonal working capital build and £106.9m acquisition spend on Falling Springs, Booth and Burfordville). Management maintained FY2026 guidance in line with consensus underlying EBITDA of ~£280m (range £273m–£285m).

Trading update (ten months to 31 October 2025)

The November 2025 update confirmed LFL revenue -3%, guided FY2025 underlying EBITDA to £275m–£280m (delivered at £278.8m), and flagged persistent GB/US residential weakness and infrastructure deferrals in GB/Ireland—consistent with the full-year outcome.

Trend assessment

Three-year pattern (filings): underlying EBITDA has grown from £269.9m (2024) to £278.8m (2025) despite organic volume pressure, but earnings per share have compressed (underlying EPS 34.4p → 31.8p → 9.4p H1 annualised run-rate impaired by higher interest and amortisation). Net debt has risen materially on US platform build-out (Lionmark EV US$238m; Falling Springs EV US$120m/£90m). The balance sheet remains covenant-compliant with extended facilities, but leverage is no longer conservative—H1 2026 covenant leverage of 2.1x sits at the top of management’s 1–2x target range.

Yahoo fallback note: Yahoo FCF of £105.8m for FY2025 (operating cash flow £225.9m less capex £120.1m) differs from the company’s adjusted FCF of £133.2m; all FCF figures above are from filings. Yahoo net debt (£481.1m ex-leases) aligns directionally with filing net debt ex-IFRS 16 (£481.1m at 31 Dec 2025).

Coverage gaps: Only one interim filing is indexed (H1 2026). No separate H1 2025 interim body is present; H2 2024/H1 2025 comparatives are embedded in the H1 2026 interim. Companies House annual accounts are available but add no material figures beyond the RNS Final Results. The 2025 Annual Report body in the index is a publication notice (XHTML/iXBRL availability), not a full strategic report extract—detailed risk and pension disclosures were not separately parsed from that file.
risks_and_flags:
Cyclical / market: GB remains the dominant risk. Filings describe a fourth consecutive year of volume decline in 2025 and expect a fifth in 2026, driven by residential weakness, fragile confidence and delayed project starts. Pricing came under pressure as volumes fell. Recovery timing is explicitly uncertain despite planning reforms and infrastructure pipelines (HS2 peaking, Sizewell C early-stage).

Leverage / M&A: Acquisition pace has elevated net debt and compressed ROIC. Lionmark, Falling Springs and Booth add integration and goodwill risk; H1 2026 amortisation of acquired intangibles was £10.9m. Pro-forma leverage post-Falling Springs was guided at 2.0x. Impairment headroom exists but GB sensitivities were required in FY2025.

Regulatory / competitive (cement): The “Back British Cement” campaign highlights structural threats—import share above one-third of UK cement sales, uncompetitive industrial electricity costs, uneven carbon regulation, and CBAM implementation (UK from January 2027). Breedon expects to invest over £20m in Peak Cluster/carbon capture ahead of FID. Policy failure would leave domestic producers structurally disadvantaged.

Operational: Kinnegad cement mill unscheduled shutdown (May 2026) temporarily compressed Irish margins; resolved but illustrates plant-concentration risk. US H1 2025 was disrupted by extreme Midwest weather; normalisation helped H1 2026 but residential US remains soft.

Governance / treasury: Going concern is affirmed in both annual and interim filings, with covenant compliance and liquidity under a “severe but plausible” 5–10% revenue downside. Borrowing facilities carry leverage (3.0x) and interest cover (3.5x minimum) covenants—currently comfortable (interest cover 13.5x at H1 2026). Middle East conflict flagged as an emerging risk; direct impact minimal to date per H1 2026.

Pension: No pension deficit or scheme detail appeared in the indexed filing bodies reviewed; this remains a verify-before-trade gap if the full Annual Report PDF is required.

Accounting: Restatement of cash/overdraft gross presentation (no P&L impact). Non-underlying items are significant (£34.9m FY2025; £14.6m H1 2026), largely acquisition amortisation and decarbonisation costs—underlying metrics must be read alongside statutory EPS.

RiskTags: cyclical, leverage, regulatory, competitive, accounting
news_highlights:
Coverage over the past year is moderate and skewed to results, broker reiteration and advocacy—not deep investigative journalism. Material items from `news_manifest.json` and RNS cross-reference:

- 29 July 2026 — Interim results 2026: revenue +5%, underlying EBITDA flat, dividend +5%; US/Ireland strength vs GB weakness (TradingView, Kalkine, Yahoo earnings summaries).
- 9 June 2026 — Acquisition of Falling Springs Quarry, US$120m (~£90m), 185mt reserves near St Louis (RNS; limited third-party coverage).
- 11 August 2026 — “Back British Cement” campaign update: government engagement but calls for stronger CBAM, electricity cost alignment, procurement recognition (TipRanks, TradingView).
- 11 March 2026 — FY2025 Final Results and launch of Back British Cement advocacy (Investors’ Chronicle: “Breedon struggles to escape UK construction gloom”; Armchair Trader).
- 20 November 2025 — Trading update: resilient performance, FY2025 EBITDA guide £275m–£280m (RNS).
- 29 April 2026 — AGM trading update and AGM results (RNS indexed).
- 29 July 2026 — Louis Eperjesi appointed non-executive director from early 2027 (Kalkine).
- Broker tone (July 2026): Berenberg and Deutsche Bank buy reiterations noted (MarketBeat); consensus “Moderate Buy” (MarketBeat, July 2026).
- Noise: Several Yahoo/Simply Wall St dividend and fair-value reset articles (target trims to ~£4.05–£4.50 from higher prior levels)—useful for sentiment, not primary fact.

Overall, news confirms the filing narrative (geographic divergence, M&A, UK cement policy) rather than revealing undisclosed negatives. Third-party depth is thin outside results windows.
research_rationale: Filings confirm the screen’s value and cash-return case—cheap balance sheet, strong FCF, progressive dividend and covenant headroom—but cyclical GB weakness, M&A-driven leverage and sub-target ROIC temper outright strong-buy conviction pending a UK volume inflection.
